Every once in awhile
column2: pread() or pwrite() would return EEXIST

column1: makes no sense. This turned out to be a bug in btrfs_get_extent().
Commit 8dff9c853410 (""Btrfs: deal with duplciates during extent_map
insertion in btrfs_get_extent"") fixed a case in btrfs_get_extent() where
two threads race on adding the same extent map to an inode's extent map
tree. However
column2: if the added em is merged with an adjacent em in the

column1: extent tree
column2: then we'll end up with an existing extent that is not

column1: identical to but instead encompasses the extent we tried to add. When we
call merge_extent_mapping() to find the nonoverlapping part of the new
em
column2: the arithmetic overflows because there is no such thing. We then end

column1: up trying to add a bogus em to the em_tree
that can bubble all the way up to userspace.
Fix it by extending the identical extent map special case.
